content: The global incidence and prevalence of the condition are estimated to be approximately a certain number of cases per 100,000 individuals worldwide. The prevalence of the condition is estimated to occur in a specific number of cases annually. The case-fatality rate or mortality rate associated with the condition is approximately a certain percentage. Patients of all age groups may develop the condition. However, the incidence increases with age, with the median age at diagnosis being a specific number of years. The condition commonly affects individuals either younger than or older than a certain age range. It is often first diagnosed in a particular age group. There is no racial predilection for the condition. However, individuals of a specific race are more or less likely to develop it. The condition affects men and women equally. However, it may be more commonly observed in one gender than the other, with a male-to-female or female-to-male ratio of approximately a specific value to 1.
